record.paper_title: Stationary solutions of the axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov system: present status and open problems
record.original_question: Which choices and combinations of ansatz functions Φ(E,L_z), where E is particle energy and L_z is axial angular momentum, produce convergent stationary Einstein-Vlasov solutions with spindle-like, toroidal, or composite morphologies, and do the resulting spatial densities resemble observed composite astrophysical objects such as prolate spindle-like galaxies, active-galactic-nucleus tori, disk galaxies with central bulges, dark-matter halos, or ring galaxies?

evidence.quote: In order to construct stationary solutions it is useful to make an ansatz for the density function f on phase space, namely we assume that f depends only on the particle energy E and angular momentum Lz about the axis f(x, p) = KΦ(E, Lz).

In view of the observational evidence of these types of objects we find that a more careful study of spindle solutions and toroidal solutions is motivated, where the features of the numerical solutions should be compared with the features of the observed objects.

In 2017 galaxy surveys revealed that prolate spindle-like galaxies are much more common than previously thought [47]. In 2019 it was announced that the VLA telescope had directly imaged a toroidal structure within an active galactic nucleus [23].

It turns out to be sensitive to combine ansatz functions. Our numerical algorithm does not converge for an arbitrary non-trivial linear combination of ansatz functions even if they individually give rise to solutions.
An open issue is to understand which combinations of ansatz functions give rise to composite solutions and to find out if these solutions resemble the morphology of composite objects found in nature.
Examples of composite astrophysical objects are numerous, and include disk galaxies with a central bulge, galaxies with dark matter halos, as well as ring galaxies.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the axially symmetric, stationary Einstein-Vlasov system in general relativity, in which a collisionless ensemble of particles is described by a non-negative phase-space density f(x,p) on the cotangent bundle of a four-dimensional Lorentzian spacetime admitting a timelike Killing vector field ∂_t and an axial Killing vector field ∂_φ. Along geodesics, the particle energy E = -p_t and the axial angular momentum L_z = p_φ are conserved. Restrict attention to ansätze of the form

   f(x,p) = K · Φ(E, L_z),

where K > 0 is a normalization constant and Φ : ℝ × ℝ → [0,∞) is a measurable function (the "ansatz function"). The induced spatial mass density ρ is obtained by integrating f over the momentum fiber, and the metric is determined self-consistently from the Einstein field equations sourced by the resulting energy-momentum tensor.

Problems:

(a) Determine which classes of ansatz functions Φ(E, L_z), and which (nontrivial) linear or non-linear combinations of such functions, yield convergent stationary axisymmetric solutions of the Einstein-Vlasov system whose spatial density ρ has one of the following morphologies:
   (i) a prolate "spindle" concentrated along the axis of symmetry;
   (ii) a "toroidal" support encircling the axis with a central hole;
   (iii) a composite morphology combining the above with disk-like or bulge-like components, including ring-shaped supports and halo-type extended supports.

(b) For the convergent solutions in (a), characterize quantitatively the resulting density profiles (e.g., aspect ratios, equatorial-to-polar extent, hole sizes, mass concentrations) and decide whether they reproduce the morphological features attributed to physical configurations such as prolate spindle-like galaxies, active-galactic-nucleus tori, disk galaxies with central bulges, dark-matter halos, or ring galaxies.

(c) Provide a mathematical criterion explaining why arbitrary nontrivial linear combinations of individually admissible ansatz functions need not yield convergent stationary solutions, and identify sufficient conditions on Φ ensuring existence and convergence.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as part of a survey of open problems on stationary solutions of the axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov system. No subsequent work appears to give a general classification of ansatz functions Φ(E,L_z) producing convergent spindle, toroidal, or composite morphologies; existing studies (Andréasson, Ames, Logg and collaborators) provide numerical examples but no systematic existence/classification result. The problem appears to remain open.
